commits.message:
fix(email-parsing): close the gap where the LLM fallback never engages, plus concrete extraction bugs

Reported by the user against a real production email (jobs.nvoids.com
relay, "Java Developer onsite omaha ne no"): company came back as the
entire "MUST HAVE" skills paragraph, location came back as "Omaha,
NE- 100" (the "100% onsite" percentage bleeding into the value), and
required_skills included a spurious ".NET" the email never mentions.
Checked the last 5 postings and then all of production: 94 of the last
105 job-requirement drafts (90%) had a null company field. This is not
a handful of edge cases -- it's the normal shape of these emails.

Root cause, the big one: the deterministic parser's confidence score
(app/email_parsing/parsers.py) only ever looked at job_title and
required_skills evidence. A posting with a clear title and a real
skills list scored 0.92 -- comfortably above FALLBACK_CONFIDENCE_
THRESHOLD (0.70) -- even with company null, so the LLM fallback
(app/email_parsing/llm_fallback.py, already wired to LiteLLM/Langfuse,
already credentialed in production, already forcing live mode via
force_live=True regardless of HERMES_PROMPT_RUNTIME_DRY_RUN) never
got a chance to fill in exactly the field it exists to fill: a company
named in free-text prose ("Hi, this is Francis from Indus River
Technologies...") rather than under a "Company:" label, which is what
COMPANY_PATTERN's label-based regex requires and most vendor/recruiter
templates simply don't use. Confidence now caps at 0.65 -- below the
fallback threshold -- when title and skills are both present but
company is not, routing these into the fallback without changing
scoring for postings that are genuinely incomplete on title/skills.
Added a "company_missing" warning alongside the existing ones.

Three more concrete, independently-caused bugs found while digging
through this same production email:

- app/email_parsing/signature.py: COMPANY_SUFFIX_RE/TITLE_KEYWORDS_RE
  were matched against full lines with no length bound, so "...
  MESSAGING SERVICES EXPERIENCE SUCH AS KAFKA ..." matched on the word
  "services" and the entire multi-line skills dump became the
  company_name. A real signature company/title line is short; lines
  over 80 chars are now skipped as candidates.

- app/understanding/parsers/job_description_fields.py: LOCATION_
  PATTERN's \s* between the label's colon and its value could cross a
  newline, so a blank templated "Location:\nLinkedIn:\n..." field (the
  recruiter's own "please fill this in" placeholder) swallowed the
  next label's name as if it were the location. The value now has to
  start on the same line as the label, so an empty occurrence is
  skipped in favor of a real one later in the email. Separately, a
  trailing "- 100[%]" or "- onsite/hybrid/remote" qualifier (location
  regex has to allow digits/dashes for values like "I-95 corridor", so
  it can't just exclude them) is now trimmed after the fact.

- app/understanding/parsers/skills.py: fuzzy_match_terms() allowed
  4-character terms into fuzz.partial_ratio matching against the whole
  email body. partial_ratio scores a needle against its best-matching
  substring anywhere in the haystack, and the shorter the needle the
  more likely a long email coincidentally scores >=94 somewhere.
  ".NET" (normalized "net") is the confirmed case; raised the floor to
  6 characters, which is exactly long enough to exclude this class
  while leaving fuzzy matching for actual typo recovery on longer
  terms ("Kubernetes"/"Kubernets").

Also stripped the jobs.nvoids.com relay's own boilerplate ("You
received this email from X via https://jobs.nvoids.com. Please check
the email id...") from job_description, alongside the existing
From:/Sent:/To:/Subject: forwarded-header strip -- same "only at the
very top" rule, so real body content using the same words mid-email is
untouched.

New/updated coverage: hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py gains the full
nvoids Java-posting fixture as a named regression (location, .NET
false-positive, preamble strip, confidence-below-threshold) plus a
"Location: / LinkedIn:" blank-template-field case; the existing
"complete requirement" fixture now includes a Company: line so it
stays genuinely complete under the new scoring, with a paired new case
asserting a title+skills-but-no-company posting requires review.
hermes-850-email-signature-check.py gains the MUST-HAVE-paragraph-as-
company-name case. Full regression suite (16 checks) green against a
freshly reset schema.
